[USER] User expressed interest in the origins of the popular Vietnamese coffee blend and how it is traditionally served.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The popular Vietnamese coffee blend, known as Cà phê sữa đá, originated during the French colonial period in the late 19th century.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The French introduced coffee to Vietnam, which became popular, but locals mixed it with condensed milk to make it more affordable.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The traditional way to serve Vietnamese coffee is to brew it using a small metal drip filter called a phin filter.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Coffee is brewed with hot water, and a small amount of condensed milk is added to the cup before the coffee is poured in.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The coffee is stirred to combine with the condensed milk, creating a rich, sweet, and creamy drink.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To serve it iced, coffee is brewed directly into a glass filled with ice cubes, and condensed milk is added before the hot coffee is poured in.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The drink is stirred to combine and chilled for a refreshing coffee beverage.  
[USER] User expressed enthusiasm about the taste of Vietnamese coffee.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some coffee shops offer Vietnamese coffee, but it may not be as widely available as other types.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Vietnamese coffee is a unique and flavorful experience worth trying.
